clue.text: Film my new gravel net working

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are put to work and set going in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone at work on a new net for gravel, maybe a builder sieving stones.
explanation.walkthrough: All fourteen letters of MY NEW GRAVEL NET are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve Angry Men is the 1957 courtroom drama starring Henry Fonda as a dissenting juror.

clue.text: Power to restrain rare swimming voles

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold in, so the power letters enclose the others

parts.note: watts are units of power

indicators.note: swimming suggests letters moving about, so rare is rearranged

explanation.surface: Something powerful to control unusual voles out swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' seems to describe the voles but is the signal to shuffle rare; the power unit is plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Water rat is the common name for the water vole, a riverbank rodent.

clue.text: Possibly Harold's Dolly Mixture

definitions.note: the definition reads as the surname that may follow Harold, as with the actor

indicators.note: a mixture blends the letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Harold's bag of Dolly Mixtures, a British children's sweet of small sugary pastel shapes.
explanation.walkthrough: Dolly Mixture is a British assortment of tiny sweets; here 'Mixture' rearranges DOLLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Lloyd was the silent-film comedian famous for hanging from a clock face, so the surname could be Harold's.

clue.text: Vulnerabilities certain trade shows must cover

indicators.note: to cover something is to go round it, so the shows enclose the certain word

parts.note: expos are exhibitions or trade fairs
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Trade fairs are obliged to protect against known weaknesses.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposures are states of being unprotected or open to harm, the same as weak points.

clue.text: Network parts new poems

parts.note: odes are lyric poems

explanation.surface: Pieces of a network presented as fresh pieces of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodes are the points in a network where connections meet, its component junctions.

clue.text: Bringing back engineers on the telephone

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
someone calling is on the phone

explanation.surface: Engineers being recalled by phone to fix a fault.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Recalling means summoning someone back, or bringing a memory back to mind.

clue.text: New vaccine technology cracked by unknown actress essential to 3

indicators.note: being cracked by something means it breaks in, so the unknown goes inside

parts.note: mRNA vaccines, using messenger RNA, were the novel technology of the Covid pandemic
in algebra an unknown is x, y or z; here Y

explanation.surface: A modern vaccine breakthrough cracked open by a mystery performer.
explanation.walkthrough: Myrna Loy was a Hollywood actress; LOY sits in the middle of the answer to 3, LLOYD.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrna Loy starred in The Thin Man, and her surname is the core of the Harold actor's surname at 3.

clue.text: Presents include second house which didn't turn up

indicators.note: include means the presents take the other letters inside them

parts.note: the present is now, so presents (present times) are nows

explanation.surface: Gifts include a second house, but the guests never arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Presents' looks like gifts but means present moments, NOWS.
explanation.definitionFit: No-shows are people who fail to arrive for an appointment or booking; the definition describes them.

clue.text: These cut some grass

definitions.meaning: first meaning: cutting edges, as on knives or mowers
second meaning: individual leaves of grass

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a gardener mowing a lawn; the plural noun names both cutters and slim leaves of grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Blades are the sharp edges of tools, and also the narrow leaves of grass plants.

clue.text: Group heading for draw

parts.note: a lot is a group or batch of items, as at an auction
heading for a place means going to it

explanation.surface: A band setting off towards some event, perhaps a raffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a lottery game, in which winning numbers are picked out in a draw.

clue.text: Rude Spice's unusual foot treatments

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters appear in an out-of-the-ordinary order

parts.note: the word Spice gives its letters; the apostrophe-s is the link 'has' or 'is'

explanation.surface: A Spice Girl, cheekily nicknamed Rude Spice, has odd beauty routines for her feet.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of RUDE SPICE are rearranged; the 's is read as 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedicures are cosmetic care sessions for the feet and toenails.

clue.text: Mocks dried-out enchantress's clothes

indicators.note: out, as in 'dried-out', means the letters are put out of their order
the clothes of a word are its outside letters, wrapping the rest

explanation.surface: Someone ridicules a sorceress for her shrivelled, dried-out garments.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 'dried-out' splits: 'out' shuffles dried, and the enchantress's 'clothes' are her first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To deride someone is to ridicule or scoff at them, the same as mocking.

clue.text: Spanish army guy promoted at a party

parts.note: to promote a product or idea is to sell it, so promoted gives sold
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A Spanish soldier gets a promotion while attending a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldado is the Spanish word for soldier, so a Spanish army man.

clue.text: Did butterfly start to pollute bog?

parts.note: to do butterfly is to swim that stroke, so did butterfly means swam

indicators.note: the start to a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A question whether a butterfly began contaminating a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butterfly' looks like the insect but is the swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A swamp is a stretch of wet, waterlogged ground, which is what a bog is.

clue.text: Bomb nuclear reactor broken by nearly-new software

indicators.note: broken by means the reactor is split open to let other letters in

parts.note: an early nuclear reactor was called an atomic pile

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter of new is missing

parts.note: taken as written, then cut short
an app is a software application

explanation.surface: A nuclear reactor is disabled by an almost brand-new software program, ending in an explosion.
explanation.walkthrough: An early reactor was called an atomic pile; 'nearly-new' splits so that 'nearly' trims new.
explanation.definitionFit: Pineapple is military slang for a hand grenade, from its segmented casing.

clue.text: Eats in lines, causing unruly behaviour

indicators.note: in means one set of letters is placed within the other

parts.note: rows are lines of seats, people or things
to dine is to eat a meal, so eats gives dines

explanation.surface: Diners eating in long lines at a canteen lead to rowdy scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdiness is noisy, disorderly conduct, such as a boisterous crowd displays.

clue.text: Shelter one of 40 asleep, hiding straggly beard

indicators.note: hiding means the wink conceals the other letters inside it

parts.note: forty winks is a short nap, so one of them is a wink

indicators.note: a straggly beard is untidy, so its letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A dozing man with an unkempt beard takes cover.
explanation.walkthrough: Forty winks is a nap; 'straggly' turns BEARD into DBREA, which WINK hides.
explanation.definitionFit: A windbreak is a fence, hedge or screen giving protection from the wind.

clue.text: Skinny dip with me — real kinky!

definitions.note: read as 'of the skin', an adjective

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters are bent out of order

explanation.surface: An invitation to a saucy skinny-dip, keeping it real.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinny' looks like part of skinny-dip but is the definition: relating to skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Epidermal means relating to the epidermis, the outer layer of skin, hence humorously skin-y.

clue.text: Rebellions at New York office a daily event

parts.note: risings are uprisings or revolts
the United Nations has its headquarters in New York, abbreviated UN

explanation.surface: News of uprisings reaching a New York office every day.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun comes up each morning, so its appearance over the horizon happens every day.

clue.text: Depletes stock as hunters fail to keep up

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a hunter is a pocket watch with a hinged cover

explanation.walkthrough: The hunters look like people chasing game, but a hunter is a kind of pocket watch; the letters split differently for each meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Watches that lose time run slow; supplies that dwindle run low, with the letters regrouped.

clue.text: Medal keeps one operational

indicators.note: keeps means the medal holds the other letter inside it

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal or decoration
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: An award winner holding on to a medal that still works.
explanation.walkthrough: GONG is British informal slang for a medal or honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A going concern is a working one; going means up and running, functioning.

clue.text: The moment king enters, fetch seal

indicators.note: enters means the moment and king go inside the other word

parts.note: to fetch is to go and get
as means at the moment when, as in 'as he arrived'
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: As soon as the king comes in, someone is told to bring the royal seal.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasket is a ring or sheet that makes a tight joint, sealing it.

clue.text: Win deal to scramble a type of egg

indicators.note: to scramble is to jumble up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Win a deal for eggs and scramble them, a breakfast scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scramble' plays on cooking eggs, but signals the letters of WIN DEAL being mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A new-laid egg is a very fresh one, just produced by the hen, a description used as a kind.

clue.text: Vehicle was first to carry silver

indicators.note: to carry means the winning word holds the silver inside

parts.note: to come first in a contest is to win, so was first gives won
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A cart that won a race and was laden with silver.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon is a four-wheeled cart or a railway goods truck, a kind of transport.

clue.text: Tendency of apparently unipedal medic?

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
a one-footed being has one foot: I (Roman one) and FT (foot)

explanation.surface: A question about the leanings of a one-legged doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke imagines a doctor with only one foot: DR plus I FT.
explanation.definitionFit: A drift is a general trend or tendency, as in the drift of an argument.

clue.text: Exchanges prison features inspiring Irish broadcaster

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the bars take the broadcaster inside

parts.note: bars are a familiar feature of prison cells
RTE is Raidió Teilifís Éireann, Ireland's national broadcaster

explanation.surface: An Irish TV company is inspired by prison life for a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: RTE is Raidió Teilifís Éireann, Ireland's public broadcaster; 'inspiring' means breathing it in.
explanation.definitionFit: To barter is to trade goods directly without money, so barters are swaps.

clue.text: Vehicles not starting fights

indicators.note: not starting means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: trucks are vehicles

explanation.surface: Cars that won't start lead to brawls among drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruck is a scrimmage or brawl, so rucks are scuffles; the rugby ruck is a loose scrum.

clue.text: Word-lover has dossier on company symbols, I hear

indicators.note: I hear says the letters are what is spoken aloud, not what is spelt

parts.note: a dossier is a file; company symbols are logos; file placed on, after, logo gives the spoken form

explanation.surface: A brand manager keeps a file about company logos.
explanation.walkthrough: LOGO followed by FILE, said aloud, gives the word for a lover of words; 'on' puts the file after the logos.
explanation.definitionFit: From Greek logos (word) and -phile (lover), a logophile is someone who loves words.

clue.text: Hollow farming equipment no longer fashionable

indicators.note: no longer means the fashionable letters are dropped from the machine's name

parts.note: a combine harvester, usually called a combine, reaps and threshes grain
in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: A farm machine described as hollow and out of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: COMBE is a British word, chiefly in the West Country, for a short valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A combe is a short valley or hollow on a hillside, a word common in English place names.

clue.text: Film director leaves halfway through talks resolving to have only one prize

parts.note: Michael Winner was an English film director, known for Death Wish

indicators.note: resolving means the letters are worked apart and settled into a new order
halfway through a word is as far as its first half, so only that half is kept

explanation.surface: A director walks out of negotiations midway as they are settled, leaving only one award.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Winner directed Death Wish. 'halfway through' keeps the first half of leaves, which joins talks before 'resolving' shuffles the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A winner-takes-all contest gives the whole reward to the single victor, with nothing for runners-up.
